Bachelor of Engineering (Biomedical Engineering)

1st & 2nd Semester

1st SEMESTER

Common to Aerospace, Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical, Industrial and Mechanical Engineering Programs

REQUIRED:
Introduction to Engineering
* Writing Skills
General Chemistry
Calculus I
Linear Algebra
Physics: Mechanics

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table A .
* This course is graded on a pass/fail basis.

2nd SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
* Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
Digital Computation and Programming
Principles of Engineering Economics
Electric Circuit Analysis
Calculus II
Physics: Waves and Fields

* This course is graded on a pass/fail basis.

3rd & 4th Semester

3rd SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Biology I
Biomedical Physics
Statics and Mechanics of Materials
Digital Systems
Differential Equations and Vector Calculus

NOTE: All required courses in 1st and 2nd semester are requisites to all required courses in 3rd semester.

4th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Physiology
Biomechanics
Biomaterials
Communication in the Engineering Professions
Electronics and Sensors

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table A .

5th & 6th Semester

5th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Anatomy
Bioinformatics
Introduction to Software
Fluid Mechanics
Signals and Systems I
Microprocessor Systems

6th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Signals and Systems II
Control Systems and Bio-Robotics
Biomedical Instrumentation
Electric Machines and Actuators
Statistics

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table B .

NOTE: Students who have a CLEAR Academic Standing may opt to enroll in the Industrial Internship Program (IIP). Eligible students should select WKT 99A/B on the course intention form.

7th & 8th Semester

7th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
* Biomedical Eng Capstone Design

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from the following:

Science Fiction
Technology and the Contemporary Environment
Scientific Technology and Modern Society
Religion, Science and Philosophy
Power, Change and Technology
PROFESSIONAL: Four courses from the following:

Tissue Engineering
Radiation Therapy Devices
Rehabilitation Engineering
Biomedical Signal Analysis

* BME 700 has a GPA weight of 0.50.

NOTE: BME 700 and BME 800 must be taken within the same academic year.
8th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
* Biomedical Eng Capstone Design
Law and Ethics in Engineering Practice
PROFESSIONAL: Three courses from the following:
Human-Computer Interaction
Design of Bio-MEMS
Computations in Genetic Engineering
Biomedical Systems Modelling
Biomedical Image Analysis

* BME 800 has a GPA Weight of 1.50.
NOTE: BME 700 and BME 800 must be taken within the same academic year.
